findings.description: The new auth.json rewrite only replaces tokens.refresh_token. Every other field of the host's ~/.codex/auth.json is copied verbatim into $HOME_DIR/.codex/auth.json, which is bind-mounted read-write at /home/evaluser inside the container where the agent under evaluation runs with network access. That includes tokens.access_token (a live bearer usable against the OpenAI API until exp), tokens.id_token (an OIDC identity token carrying the account's email/account_id), and OPENAI_API_KEY when auth_mode is api-key. The test fixture happens to use OPENAI_API_KEY: null, so the suite never exercises the case where a long-lived API key is present. Unlike the refresh token, an API key is not single-use or time-bounded, and the KF-048 pre-flight in run-ablation.sh does nothing to bound it. The agent being graded can read and exfiltrate these values; the code comment frames the change as a credential-safety fix but it only closes the refresh-token reuse hazard, not disclosure.
findings.failure_mode: An evaluated agent (or any prompt-injected content it processes from the task tree) reads /home/evaluser/.codex/auth.json and exfiltrates the host operator's OpenAI access token, identity token, or long-lived API key.
findings.suggested_fix: Minimize the copied object instead of copying everything: build a new dict containing only the keys the codex CLI needs for the dissent call (e.g. auth_mode, tokens.access_token, tokens.account_id, the placeholder refresh_token), drop id_token, and refuse or blank OPENAI_API_KEY (emit a WARN and exit 3 if it is non-null) so a long-lived key never enters the sandbox. Add a bats case with a non-null OPENAI_API_KEY asserting it does not reach the snapshot. Longer term, mint a per-run scoped key or proxy the codex call from the host so no bearer lives in the agent-writable mount.

findings.description: spend_charge now accepts a fourth argument <cap> and budget_gate a fourth <reserve-per-trial>, both substituted straight into fadd/awk arithmetic without the numeric check that is applied to <cost> on the next line. Today the only callers pass values that were validated with usd_ok in run-ablation.sh, but the library's contract (shared with other runners per the header comment) now has an unvalidated numeric input whose failure mode is silent corruption of SPENT, i.e. the --max-usd spend cap stops working rather than erroring.
findings.failure_mode: A runner passes an empty or non-numeric cap (e.g. a jq null rendered as the string "null"), fadd yields 0 or garbage, SPENT under-counts and the batch overruns --max-usd without a cut.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate cap and per with the same regex used for cost and fall back to RUN_CAP (and log) when they fail, or die, so a bad cap cannot silently disable the spend gate.

findings.description: The new grader step deletes agent-authored files by basename across the entire graded tree, not only test modules in test directories. The reserved set is every .py basename from any hidden overlay dest plus every .py under any directory that has a 'tests' or 'test' path component in the fixture (so helper modules like tests/helpers.py or tests/utils.py reserve 'helpers.py' and 'utils.py' globally). An agent's legitimate src/pkg/helpers.py therefore gets unlinked before the test command runs, and a correct solution is graded as failing with only a side-file record. The intended problem (pytest default-mode basename clash) only arises for modules pytest actually collects (test_*.py / *_test.py under rootdir-less dirs), so the rule is far broader than the hazard. Symlink handling is correct (os.walk followlinks=False, unlink removes the link not the target), so there is no escape from the tree.
findings.failure_mode: Grader silently removes non-test agent files that share a basename with a fixture or hidden helper module, producing false failures in the ablation rows and biasing the eval, with no gate that flags the row as degraded.
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict the reserved set to basenames pytest would collect (matching python_files, default test_*.py and *_test.py) and restrict removal candidates to files that would be collected by the task's test_command path; or, instead of deleting, rename the colliding agent file out of pytest's glob and record it. Surface colliding_tests_removed > 0 as a degraded/needs-review flag on the row.
